_meta.indication: REVUFORJ is a menin inhibitor indicated for the treatment of relapsed or refractory acute leukemia with a lysine methyltransferase 2A gene (KMT2A) translocation in adult and pediatric patients 1 year and older.

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, Phase 1-2, multiple-cohort, multicenter trial of revumenib monotherapy; the Phase 2 portion had three single-arm disease-based cohorts (2A KMT2Ar ALL/MPAL, 2B KMT2Ar AML, 2C NPM1c AML), each using a Simon 2-stage design to target a 25% CR/CRh rate and exclude a 10% rate.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult and pediatric patients at least 30 days old with relapsed or refractory acute leukemia with a KMT2A rearrangement (KMT2At); the pivotal analysis pooled Cohorts 2A+2B.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: The primary efficacy endpoint for Phase 2 was the rate of complete remission (CR) or CR with partial hematologic recovery (CRh).
pivotal_trials.n: 57 participants in the Pivotal Cohort (44 adults, 13 pediatric) for the interim analysis; the broader Efficacy Cohort included 104 participants.
pivotal_trials.result: In the Pivotal Cohort (N=57) the CR+CRh rate was 22.8% (95% CI 12.7, 35.8; p-value 0.0036), crossing the prespecified efficacy boundary, with a median duration of CR/CRh of 6.4 months (95% CI 3.4, NR). In the FDA Efficacy Cohort (N=104) the CR/CRh rate was 21% (95% CI 13.8, 30.3), the median duration of CR/CRh was 6.4 months (95% CI 2.7, NE), and the rate of conversion to 56-day transfusion independence (TI-56) was 14% (95% CI 8, 24).

key_safety: Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 4 (3%) patients (2 differentiation syndrome, 1 hemorrhage, 1 sudden death); serious adverse reactions in 99 (73%). Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) included hemorrhage (53%), nausea (51%), musculoskeletal pain (42%), infection (41%), diarrhea (30%). Differentiation syndrome occurred in 29% and QTc prolongation in 29%.
target_moa: Revumenib is a menin inhibitor that inhibits the interaction of both wild-type KMT2A and KMT2A fusion proteins with menin; binding of KMT2A fusion proteins with menin activates a leukemogenic transcriptional pathway in acute leukemias with KMT2A translocations.
modality: Small molecule (orally available small molecule menin inhibitor).

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: DIFFERENTIATION SYNDROME — Differentiation syndrome, which can be fatal, has occurred with REVUFORJ. If differentiation syndrome is suspected, immediately initiate corticosteroid therapy and hemodynamic monitoring until symptom resolution.

rems.type: A REMS is not necessary; management of risks will be communicated through labeling.

companion_dx_detail: No companion diagnostic was approved with this application; the Division determined a CDx would be needed and the Applicant committed to develop one postmarketing. KMT2A rearrangements are detected in routine karyotyping in the diagnostic work-up of leukemia.

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not discussed by an Advisory Committee because review did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues unexpected for a drug of this class and for treatment of patients with acute leukemia.

description.text: Added new indication for relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia with a susceptible NPM1 mutation in adult and pediatric patients 1 year and older

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for a new indication for the treatment of relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia with a susceptible nucleophosmin 1 (NPM1) mutation in adult and pediatric patients 1 year and older who have no satisfactory alternative treatment options.

orphan_indication.text: Revumenib was granted orphan drug designation on 21 Apr 2020.

citations.quote: 21 Apr 2020	Revumenib granted orphan drug designation.

summary.text: NDA 218944 was a Type 1 original NDA for a new molecular entity submitted under 505(b)(1) and reviewed under Priority review; revumenib had been granted orphan drug designation. Approval was a traditional (full) approval based on substantial evidence of effectiveness from Study SNDX-5613-0700, not an accelerated approval.

citations.quote: Revumenib is a new molecular entity. NDA 218944 for the oral tablets was submitted under the 505(b)(1) pathway for the proposed indication of treatment of adult and pediatric patients with relapsed or refractory acute leukemia with a lysine methyltransferase 2A gene rearrangement (KMT2Ar)
21 Apr 2020	Revumenib granted orphan drug designation.

The results from the Efficacy Cohort of Study SNDX-5613-0700 and the additional confirmatory data are considered substantial evidence of effectiveness of revumenib for treatment of R/R acute leukemia with a KMT2At.

requirement.text: 4730-1 Conduct a clinical trial to assess and further characterize known serious risks related to the use of revumenib of sudden death, QTc prolongation, differentiation syndrome and elevated transaminases, and assess serious potential risks such as elevated parathyroid hormone. The trial will determine whether long-term use of revumenib is associated with increased risk of cardiac deaths, recurrent differentiation syndrome, serious hepatotoxicity, and serious potential risk of endocrine-related disorders due to chronic menin inhibition. All patients should have at least 3 years of treatment or discontinued earlier.
